title: Ethics in conversation: Building an ethics assurance case for autonomous AI-enabled voice agents in healthcare

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated qualitatively through multi-disciplinary workshops applying a principles-based ethics assurance argument to identify the risk of marginalizing patients whose native language is not English.

Assessed via semi-structured expert discussions and a 'reflective equilibrium' decision procedure to identify the potential entrenchment of inequalities for socially isolated patients, those less comfortable using telephones, or those with complex healthcare needs.

Identified as a potential risk originating from the use of pre-trained language models and human judgment in patient selection, analyzed using Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA) and ethics assurance risk matrices.
